title: One Sun, seven bands
summary: Seven stops through the SDO bands of 10 May 2024, from the Earth-facing disk to an active region and the limb, ending with free band switching.

stops.title: One Sun, seven bands
stops.body: This is the Earth-facing disk of the Sun on 10 May 2024, around 12:00 UTC, in visible light. Mostly the photosphere, the Sun's visible surface, shown in gray. Seven frames, one per band, were taken within about 30 seconds. Colors are assigned to the AIA bands.

sources.label: Helioviewer JP2 header of the HMI frame
SDO channels page
SDO AIA and HMI color names
Schou et al. 2012, HMI instrument paper

stops.title: Active region 13664
stops.body: NOAA active region 13664 is on the disk, lower right. This band shows mostly the photosphere, log T 3.7 (about 5,000 K). Sunspots look dark because they are cooler than the gas around them. The next three stops stay on this same place, in bands of different characteristic temperature.

sources.label: NOAA SWPC Solar Region Summary, 10 May 2024
NOAA SWPC Solar Region Summary, 11 May 2024
SDO channels page

stops.title: 304 Å, the same view
stops.body: Extreme ultraviolet, 304 Å: the chromosphere and transition region, light from He II, log T 4.7 (about 50,000 K). This is cooler than the 171 Å band that follows. Red is an assigned color.

sources.label: SDO channels page

stops.title: 171 Å, active region 13664
stops.body: Extreme ultraviolet, 171 Å: light from Fe IX, log T 5.8 (about 630,000 K), the temperature of the quiet corona and upper transition region. Gold is an assigned color.

sources.label: SDO channels page

stops.title: 211 Å, active region 13664
stops.body: Extreme ultraviolet, 211 Å: the corona over active regions, light from Fe XIV, log T 6.3 (about 2 million K). Purple is an assigned color.

sources.label: SDO channels page
Lemen et al. 2012, AIA instrument paper
SDO AIA and HMI color names

stops.title: Past the edge
stops.body: Extreme ultraviolet, 193 Å: the corona, light from Fe XII, log T 6.1 (about 1.3 million K), a little cooler than 211 Å. Here the glow reaches past the Sun's visible edge, because hot gas above the limb shines there too; switch to HMI to see where the visible edge is. Bronze is an assigned color.

sources.label: SDO channels page

stops.title: Your turn
stops.body: Now the bands are yours. Switch freely between all seven, including 1700 Å, ultraviolet continuum from the photosphere and temperature minimum, and 94 Å, mostly flaring regions of the corona, log T 6.8 (about 6.3 million K). Pink and green are assigned colors.
